# skill-mcp **English** · [Русский](README.ru.md) Your agent has hundreds of skills and ignores them — this hands it the right one, the rest stay out of context. [![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![node: 20 or newer](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A5%2020-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org) [![runtime dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime_dependencies-0-brightgreen.svg)](package.json) A local MCP server and an opencode plugin. It indexes the `SKILL.md` files already on your machine, searches them when a message arrives, and puts the candidates plus the likely match into the request context. No network, no API keys, no model of its own. The problem it solves: at each model step opencode lists every registered skill as id, name and description, and nothing more (see the skills guide under Loading). A skill whose description does not overlap the request stays invisible, and a message with no auto-match reads as if no skills exist, so the agent answers from general knowledge instead of opening the skill that fits. ## Demo ![skill-mcp demo: the full 416-skill catalog is 195,639 chars (~52,488 tokens) per request, the plugin hint is 1,380 chars (~411 tokens) and forms in 4.9 ms](assets/gitshow/demo.png) Two panels from one measured run on 13.11.2026. Left: the catalog of 416 skills in the XML form opencode sends, 195,639 characters or about 52,488 tokens, paid on every request. Right: what the plugin adds for one message, 1,380 characters or about 411 tokens, built in 4.9 ms against a 150 ms budget. Under them are the two parts the plugin emits: the router rule (442 characters) and the `` block for a Russian contract-review query (938 characters, 4 candidates), copied from the run without edits. Both token counts use one estimate, ASCII characters divided by 4 plus non-ASCII divided by 3, so read them as a ratio rather than a tokenizer's answer. The image is assembled from the measured parts, not a terminal screenshot; the terminal run behind the index is below. `node cli/smoke.mjs` on 13.11.2026: 416 `SKILL.md` found under 4 roots, index built in 760.7 ms, 5 queries with their top three and the fields that matched. The last query is Russian and comes back in Russian, because the index keeps both sides of the bridge. ## What you get **The search runs before the answer.** A fixed rule goes to the front of the system prompt on every owner message and makes `find` the agent's first action. The gate backs it in code: until a `find` call is seen for the current message, every other tool call of the main session is refused (`plugin/hint.mjs:89-93`, `plugin/gate.mjs:12-14`). **One hint instead of the whole catalog.** 1,380 characters (about 411 tokens) against 195,639 characters (about 52,488 tokens) for 416 skills: 52,077 tokens saved on a request, 99.2% less. With the body of the top skill preloaded (11,530 characters, about 3,565 tokens) the request carries about 3,976 tokens, which is still 92.4% less than the catalog. The catalog figure is the XML form of the same list opencode builds, measured on 13.11.2026 with the estimate above. **Candidates arrive inside the same request.** The hint holds up to 5 candidates in 1000 characters and is built within 150 ms; the preload adds the body of the top confident skill up to 20000 characters (`plugin/hint.mjs:95-97,108`). The measured block used 4 candidates, 938 characters and 4.9 ms. **Search reads Russian too.** BM25 over skill name, description and headings, plus a fixed RU to EN dictionary in `core/lexicon.ru-en.json`. A Russian query about a complaint to the antitrust service returns `biased-tender-detection` first and `fas-complaint-draft` second, with the Russian stems listed in `why` (`node cli/smoke.mjs`, run of 13.11.2026). **Local and read-only by construction.** No runtime dependencies (`package.json:45`), no network call in the code, `SKILL.md` files opened read-only, and a path that resolves outside its skill root refused with `E_FORBIDDEN` (`core/sources.mjs:241`). ## Quick start Requires Node.js 20 or newer (`package.json:8`). The package is not on the npm registry: build the tarball from a checkout. ```sh git clone https://github.com/Klaus101-ai/skill-mcp.git cd skill-mcp npm install npm pack npm install -g ./skill-finder-mcp-.tgz skill-finder-mcp init ``` `npm pack` prints the file name with the version from `package.json:3`. `init` finds your opencode config, adds `mcp.skill-mcp` as a local stdio server and the plugin entry, prints the diff and saves a `.bak-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` copy before writing (`cli/main.mjs`). JSONC comments survive the edit, and a second run changes nothing. Then check the whole chain and restart opencode: ```sh skill-finder-mcp doctor ``` `doctor` checks Node, the config file, the MCP entry and the server file it points at, the plugin entry and the `index.mjs` inside the plugin directory, the skill roots and a probe search. Exit code 0 means every check passed (`cli/main.mjs`). ## Hide the built-in skill list The list costs more than the hint. opencode writes the id, name and description of every permitted skill into the model's context at each step, and the 52,488-token figure above is that list for 416 skills. Two supported ways take it out, and skill-mcp keeps working with either. There is no key that only stops the list. The `skills` array in `opencode.json` adds sources, it does not hide anything (`@opencode/schema/dist/config.d.ts:69`). **1. Deny the `skill` action.** All skills leave the model's list, and loading by ID is rejected: ```json { "permissions": [ { "action": "skill", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" } ] } ``` Rules run in order and the last match wins, so a narrower `allow` placed after this line lets one skill back in. The shape of the triple is in the config schema (`@opencode/schema/dist/config.d.ts:47-55`), the behaviour in the skills guide under [Permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills). The agent can still read a skill body through `outline` and `read-section`, which open the file themselves (`server/index.mjs:100,113`). **2. Mark skills `autoinvoke: false`.** The skill stays registered and loadable by ID, and drops out of the model's list. In a skill's frontmatter: ```yaml metadata: opencode/autoinvoke: false ``` `disable-model-invocation: true` has the same effect. From a plugin, `ctx.skill.transform(...)` sets the same field on a loaded skill and `ctx.skill.reload()` applies it (`node_modules/@opencode/plugin/dist/promise/skill.d.ts:13-14`; the field is `Skill.Info.autoinvoke` in `@opencode/schema/dist/skill.d.ts:25`). Before you switch either one on: - Built-in skills ship inside opencode and have no directory under any skill root. A deny removes them, and skill-mcp cannot index them because there is no file to walk. In the run above, all 416 indexed skills came from the four roots on disk. - skill-mcp indexes files named `SKILL.md` only (`core/sources.mjs:174`). A flat `/name.md` skill never appears in its results, and once the list is hidden it is invisible to the agent. - The roots are the six paths under Configuration, all home or project scoped. A project `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills` directory is not read, so skills that live only there have no fallback either (`core/sources.mjs:16-23`). - Restart opencode after a config change. The list is built at load, not per message. This section comes from the official documentation, read on 13.11.2026, and the permission triple was checked against the schema files. Neither recipe was exercised in a live run on this machine. ## How it works The plugin adds three things to a request, all from the same index. - `rule`: a fixed instruction block unshifted to the front of the system prompt on every owner message. It tells the agent to call `find` first and states that a missing hint block means no auto-match, not an empty skill folder. The rule fires even when nothing matched, and a marker keeps it to one copy per request. - `preload`: the body of the top confident candidate, up to 20000 characters, as a `` part. - `hint`: up to 5 candidates as a `` part, 1000 characters max, built inside a 150 ms budget. Candidates without confidence are marked in the block. The index warms up when the plugin loads, so the first request pays for a search rather than a full walk. A query that matches no skill produces no hint and no preload; the rule still goes in. ## Find gate Until a `find` call is seen for the current owner message, the main session gets every other tool call refused. The refusal starts with `skill-mcp gate` and names the call to make. These calls pass without `find`: - `sequential_thinking`, `todowrite`, `todoread`, `question`, `skill`, `subagent` and `task` (`plugin/gate.mjs:54`); - `execute` whose code calls `find`; - `execute` whose code calls `sequential_thinking` and nothing else; - every call in a subagent session, which is outside the gate. A new owner message is recognised by the number of user messages plus the text of the last one; a new signature closes the gate again. Unreadable session state or an `execute` payload the gate cannot read allows the call instead of refusing it, which is the fail-open contract (`plugin/gate.mjs:14-15`). A missing or malformed config file does not: it leaves the gate on, which is the default. `SKILL_MCP_GATE=off` or `"gate": false` removes the layer. ## MCP server tools | Tool | Arguments | Limits | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | `query` (required), `limit`, `restrict_to` | `limit` 1 to 10, default 10; `restrict_to` takes names or globs | | `outline` | `name`, or `path` to a `SKILL.md` | frontmatter plus headings with line numbers, 40 headings max, then `truncated: true` | | `read-section` | `name`, `heading`, `max_lines` | `heading` is text or its 1-based number; `max_lines` 1 to 600, default 150 | Three tools, declared in `server/index.mjs:60,100,113`. The server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio, one message per line, and exits when stdin closes. Every tool schema declares `additionalProperties: false`, and arguments are type-checked before a search runs. Failures come back either as a JSON-RPC code (-32700 through -32603) or as a tool error: `E_INVALID_INPUT`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_FORBIDDEN`, `E_SECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `E_UNAVAILABLE`. The index is built on first use and cached for the life of the process. A `find` call over stdio, as the agent makes it: ```json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"find","arguments":{"query":"review a supply contract","limit":3}}} ``` Every item carries `confident` and the skill `description`, so the model can judge the list without another call. A top-level `next` tells it what to do with the result: load the likely match, or compare the descriptions before loading. `why` names the fields that matched and the terms that hit them. ## Configuration ### Environment variables An unset variable keeps the default. `off`, `0` and `false` turn a layer off, case-insensitive. | Variable | Default | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | `SKILL_MCP_HINT` | on | off turns off the hint, the preload and the router rule | | `SKILL_MCP_PRELOAD` | on | off drops the preloaded `SKILL.md`, keeps the hint | | `SKILL_MCP_RULE` | on | off drops the router rule text only | | `SKILL_MCP_GATE` | on | off disables the find gate | | `SKILL_MCP_GATE_DEBUG` | off | `1` or `true` writes one line per gate decision to `~/.config/opencode/logs/skill-mcp-gate.log` | | `SKILL_MCP_DEBUG` | off | `1` writes plugin and server diagnostics to stderr | | `SKILL_MCP_CONFIG` | user config path | path to the plugin config file | `SKILL_MCP_RULE` and `SKILL_MCP_GATE` accept an environment value that wins over the config file. `SKILL_ROUTER_HINT` and `SKILL_ROUTER_DEBUG` still work as fallbacks when the new names are unset. ### Config file The plugin reads `~/.config/opencode/skill-mcp.config.json` unless `SKILL_MCP_CONFIG` or an explicit path says otherwise: ```json { "rule": true, "gate": true, "deny": { "build": ["experimental-*"] }, "allow": { "reviewer": ["*review*"] } } ``` `rule` and `gate` are booleans. `deny` and `allow` are maps keyed by agent id; each value lists skill names or `*` glob patterns. Deny wins over allow, and an agent with an allow list sees nothing else. A missing, unreadable or malformed file falls back to the defaults, so a config mistake never breaks a session. ### Skill roots The walker reads these directories, and only when they exist: - `~/.config/opencode/skills` - `~/.config/opencode/skill` - `~/.opencode/skills` - `~/.claude/skills` - `~/.agents/skills` - `/.opencode/skills` It skips `node_modules`, `.git` and backup directories; the match is on a whole directory name (`core/sources.mjs:11`). ## Limitations - Search is lexical. A request that shares no token with the name, description or headings of a skill will not find it. - The RU to EN bridge is a fixed dictionary in `core/lexicon.ru-en.json`. Words outside it get no translation help. - Candidate quality follows your frontmatter descriptions. A one-line description produces a thin hint. - On the final acceptance set of 60 queries, recall@5 is 0.7600, the same as the lexical baseline, and NDCG@10 is 0.6274 against 0.6654 for that baseline (`measure/README.md`). The hint and the gate are the value; the ranking is not better than BM25. - Latency figures in `measure/README.md` come from one machine and a 365-skill corpus. Treat them as a reference, not a promise. - The gate covers tool calls only. A reply written without tools is not intercepted, and the rule text is the only thing asking for a search there. - One test fails, so the suite is not green (see Development). - There is no CI workflow in the repository. Tests run where you run them. ## Troubleshooting Start with `skill-finder-mcp doctor`; it reports each piece separately and exits non-zero on a problem. A refusal that keeps coming back is a gate question, not a search question. Set `SKILL_MCP_GATE_DEBUG=1` and read one line per decision in `~/.config/opencode/logs/skill-mcp-gate.log`. The file is created only while the switch is on. No hint block in a request usually means no confident candidate for that message, or `SKILL_MCP_HINT=off` in the environment of the process that runs opencode. `SKILL_MCP_DEBUG=1` prints what the plugin decided to stderr. If you turned on the skill permission from the section above, remember that the `skill` tool no longer loads anything. The hint still points at skill names; `read-section` reads the body from disk. ## Development ```sh npm install npm run build npm test ``` `npm test` runs `node --test` over `test/`. On 13.11.2026 it reported 224 tests: 222 pass, 1 fail, 1 skipped. The failure is `test/pack.test.mjs:57`: `npm pack` picks up `README.md.bak-20261105-2124` and `README.ru.md`, both outside the allowed file set. Move the backup into `_backups/` and decide whether `README.ru.md` belongs in the package; until then the suite exits non-zero and this README does not claim otherwise. `npm run smoke` runs the smoke script, which prints the skill count, the index build time and five queries with their top three (`cli/smoke.mjs`). `npm run measure` and `npm run latency` regenerate the numbers in `measure/README.md`. The build uses esbuild with `node20` as the target and produces `dist/plugin.mjs`, `dist/plugin/index.mjs`, `dist/server.mjs`, `dist/cli.mjs` and `dist/lexicon.ru-en.json`. Design notes live in `docs/contract.md` and version history in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. ## Security and privacy The server is read-only: it opens `SKILL.md` files, never writes to them, and the CLI writes only to the opencode config and its own backup. Nothing calls the network, and no code path calls a model or another service. Paths are resolved against their root before a file is opened, so a `path` argument cannot reach outside the skill directories. Debug logs are opt-in and stay on the local disk. ## License MIT, copyright 2026 Klaus101-ai (`LICENSE`). Bundled libraries and their licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: MiniSearch 7.2.0 (MIT) and jsonc-parser 3.3.1 (MIT). esbuild is a development dependency and ships nothing.

# skill-mcp [English](README.md) · **Русский** У вашего агента сотни скиллов, и он их игнорирует — этот инструмент подаёт нужный, а остальные остаются вне контекста. [![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![node: 20 or newer](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A5%2020-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org) [![runtime dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime_dependencies-0-brightgreen.svg)](package.json) Локальный MCP-сервер и плагин для opencode. Он индексирует файлы `SKILL.md`, которые уже лежат на вашей машине, ищет по ним, когда приходит сообщение, и кладёт кандидатов вместе с вероятным совпадением в контекст запроса. Без сети, без ключей API и без собственной модели. Задача, которую он решает: на каждом шаге модели opencode перечисляет все зарегистрированные скиллы как id, название и описание, и ничего больше (раздел Loading в официальном руководстве по скиллам). Скилл, описание которого не пересекается с запросом, остаётся невидимым, а сообщение без автосовпадения выглядит так, будто скиллов нет вовсе, — и агент отвечает из общих знаний вместо того, чтобы открыть подходящий скилл. ## Демо ![Демо skill-mcp: полный каталог из 416 скиллов — 195 639 символов (≈52 488 токенов) на каждый запрос, подсказка плагина — 1 380 символов (≈411 токенов), собирается за 4,9 мс](assets/gitshow/demo.png) Две панели из одного замера 13.11.2026. Слева каталог из 416 скиллов в той XML-форме, которую отправляет opencode: 195 639 символов, примерно 52 488 токенов, и платить за него приходится на каждом запросе. Справа то, что плагин добавляет на одно сообщение: 1 380 символов, примерно 411 токенов, сборка за 4,9 мс при бюджете 150 мс. Ниже лежат обе части, которые плагин действительно выдаёт: правило-роутер (442 символа) и блок `` на русский запрос про проверку договора (938 символов, 4 кандидата), скопированные из прогона без правок. Обе оценки токенов считаются одним способом: ASCII-символы делить на 4, не-ASCII на 3. Это отношение, а не ответ токенайзера. Картинка собрана из измеренных частей, а не снята с терминала; прогон в терминале — ниже. `node cli/smoke.mjs` 13.11.2026: найдено 416 файлов `SKILL.md` в 4 корнях, индекс собран за 760,7 мс, пять запросов с тройкой первых результатов и полями, по которым они совпали. Последний запрос русский и приходит по русским словам, потому что индекс держит обе стороны моста. ## Что вы получаете **Поиск идёт до ответа.** Фиксированное правило встаёт в начало системного промпта на каждое сообщение владельца и делает `find` первым действием агента. Гейт подкрепляет это кодом: пока для текущего сообщения не увиден вызов `find`, основная сессия получает отказ на любой другой вызов инструмента (`plugin/hint.mjs:89-93`, `plugin/gate.mjs:12-14`). **Одна подсказка вместо всего каталога.** 1 380 символов (примерно 411 токенов) против 195 639 символов (примерно 52 488 токенов) на 416 скиллов: 52 077 токенов экономии на запрос, на 99,2% меньше. С предзагруженным телом лучшего скилла (11 530 символов, примерно 3 565 токенов) запрос несёт около 3 976 токенов, и это всё равно на 92,4% меньше каталога. Цифра каталога — та же XML-форма, которую строит opencode; замер 13.11.2026 тем же способом оценки. **Кандидаты приходят внутри того же запроса.** Подсказка держит до 5 кандидатов в 1000 символах и собирается за 150 мс; предзагрузка добавляет тело лучшего уверенного скилла до 20000 символов (`plugin/hint.mjs:95-97,108`). В замере вышло 4 кандидата, 938 символов и 4,9 мс. **Поиск читает и русский.** BM25 по названию, описанию и заголовкам скилла плюс фиксированный словарь RU→EN в `core/lexicon.ru-en.json`. Русский запрос про жалобу в антимонопольную службу первым отдаёт `biased-tender-detection`, вторым `fas-complaint-draft`, а русские основы перечислены в `why` (`node cli/smoke.mjs`, прогон 13.11.2026). **Локально и только на чтение по устройству.** Нулевые runtime-зависимости (`package.json:45`), ни одного сетевого вызова в коде, файлы `SKILL.md` открываются только на чтение, а путь, вышедший за свой корень, отклоняется с `E_FORBIDDEN` (`core/sources.mjs:241`). ## Быстрый старт Нужен Node.js 20 или новее (`package.json:8`). Пакета нет в реестре npm: тарболл собирается из клона. ```sh git clone https://github.com/Klaus101-ai/skill-mcp.git cd skill-mcp npm install npm pack npm install -g ./skill-finder-mcp-.tgz skill-finder-mcp init ``` `npm pack` печатает имя файла с версией из `package.json:3`. `init` находит конфиг opencode, добавляет `mcp.skill-mcp` как локальный stdio-сервер и запись плагина, печатает дифф и сохраняет копию `.bak-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` перед записью (`cli/main.mjs`). Комментарии JSONC переживают правку, а повторный запуск ничего не меняет. Затем проверьте всю цепочку и перезапустите opencode: ```sh skill-finder-mcp doctor ``` `doctor` проверяет Node, файл конфига, запись MCP и файл сервера, на который она указывает, запись плагина и `index.mjs` внутри папки плагина, корни скиллов и пробный поиск. Он велит агенту сначала вызвать `find` и отдельно говорит, что отсутствие блока-подсказки означает «автосовпадения нет», а не «папка со скиллами пуста». Правило срабатывает, даже когда ничего не нашлось, а маркер держит его в одном экземпляре на запрос. - `preload`: тело лучшего уверенного кандидата до 20000 символов как часть ``. - `hint`: до 5 кандидатов как часть ``, не больше 1000 символов, собирается в бюджете 150 мс. Кандидаты без уверенности помечены в блоке. Индекс прогревается при загрузке плагина, поэтому первый запрос платит за поиск, а не за полный обход. Запрос, который ни с чем не совпал, не даёт ни подсказки, ни предзагрузки; правило при этом остаётся. ## Гейт find Пока для текущего сообщения владельца не увиден вызов `find`, основная сессия получает отказ на каждый другой вызов инструмента. Отказ начинается со `skill-mcp gate` и называет вызов, который нужно сделать. Эти вызовы проходят без `find`: - `sequential_thinking`, `todowrite`, `todoread`, `question`, `skill`, `subagent` и `task` (`plugin/gate.mjs:54`); - `execute`, в коде которого есть вызов `find`; - `execute`, в коде которого есть только `sequential_thinking`; - любой вызов в сессии субагента: она вне гейта. Новое сообщение владельца распознаётся по числу сообщений пользователя и тексту последнего; новая подпись снова закрывает гейт. Нечитаемое состояние сессии или полезная нагрузка `execute`, которую гейт не разобрал, разрешают вызов, а не отклоняют его: так работает договор fail-open (`plugin/gate.mjs:14-15`). Отсутствующий или испорченный конфиг так не работает: гейт остаётся включённым, это и есть значение по умолчанию. `SKILL_MCP_GATE=off` или `"gate": false` снимают слой. ## Инструменты MCP-сервера | Инструмент | Аргументы | Лимиты | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | `query` (обязателен), `limit`, `restrict_to` | `limit` от 1 до 10, по умолчанию 10; `restrict_to` принимает имена или маски | | `outline` | `name` или `path` к `SKILL.md` | frontmatter и заголовки с номерами строк, не больше 40 заголовков, дальше `truncated: true` | | `read-section` | `name`, `heading`, `max_lines` | `heading` — текст или его номер с единицы; `max_lines` от 1 до 600, по умолчанию 150 | Всего три инструмента, объявлены в `server/index.mjs:60,100,113`. # measure/ — evaluation harness

## Query sets

Four query files exist and they play different roles:

- `queries.jsonl` — **draft** set (28 queries, field `relevant`). It was written
  while building the harness, to smoke-check the scripts. It is **not** for
  tuning weights, stop words or thresholds and is **not** the reported set.
- `heldout.jsonl` — **set A** (60 queries, field `qrels`, `kind` ∈
  `easy` | `hard` | `empty`). It was composed **independently** by a different
  agent and is **not** to be adjusted to the system. It was committed as
  `M4: held-out query set (independent)` **before** any measurement run, so the
  history proves the set predates the numbers.
- `heldout-b.jsonl` — **set B** (60 queries), the acceptance set (§ M8),
  committed before any run on it.
- `heldout-c.jsonl` — **set C** (60 queries), the final acceptance set
  (§ Final acceptance (set C)), committed before any run on it.

### Status change (M5): set A is now the VALIDATION set

All M4 measurements on set A are fixed (commit `bbf9c74` / `2a7766f`), so set A
can no longer serve as an honest "untouched" test: M5 changes are **verified**
against it (that is what a validation set is for). From M5 on:

- **set A = validation**: normal iteration happens here — a change is judged by
  its before/after table on A. Queries and qrels never change; weights are only
  selected through a *measured comparison on A* with the numbers recorded below
  (M5 § Weights). Two one-time, task-driven exceptions, both recorded in the
  reports: the stop list was extended to the standard service-word list in M7
  (the set files themselves stayed byte-identical), and the score threshold was
  **abolished** in M7 in favour of the coverage rule (M7 § Rule) — so there is
  no threshold left to select.
- **set B = acceptance (deferred, honest)**: an independent agent will build a
  fresh held-out set B later, with no knowledge of these numbers, and acceptance
  runs there. The formulations in `heldout.jsonl` are **not** modified — the file
  stays byte-identical to commit `bbf9c74`, so M4 and M5 numbers stay comparable.
  *Update: set B was built and measured as `heldout-b.jsonl` (§ M8), and the
  final acceptance set C as `heldout-c.jsonl` (§ Final acceptance (set C)) —
  both committed before any run on them.*

`heldout.jsonl` line shape:

```json
{"id": 1, "query": "...", "qrels": ["skill-name", ...], "kind": "easy"}
```

- `easy` (35) — one clearly named skill; `hard` (15) — two qrels, an ambiguous
  or multi-skill request; `empty` (10) — everyday questions with **no** skill
  answer (`qrels: []`), used for the AC3 block.
- `qrels` hold **skill names** (frontmatter `name`), not folder names.

## Pipeline under test (M5)

`core/index.mjs` search now runs three steps before anything is returned:

1. **Normalization + light stemming** (`core/text.mjs`): lower-case, `ё`→`е`,
   punctuation stripped, then frequent RU endings (-ами/-ями/-ов/-ев/-ий/-ый/
   -ая/-ое/-ые/-ой/-ей/-ам/-ям/-ах/-ях/-и/-ы/-а/-я/-о/-е/-у/-ю) and EN endings
   (-ing/-es/-ed/-s) are cut with a root-protection floor of 3 characters.
   The same pipeline is injected into MiniSearch as `tokenize` + `processTerm`,
   which MiniSearch applies to documents **and** to query strings — one code
   path, no drift between index and query.
2. **AC3 significant-match gate**: a result is valid only if it covers enough
   meaningful query tokens — **`≥ min(2, N)`** since M7, where N is the number
   of meaningful tokens (≥3 chars or an upper-case whitelisted acronym, not in
   the standard service-word stop list, judged after
   normalization/stemming); M5–M6 asked for **at least one**. If no skill
   covers enough, `search()` returns `[]` — the MCP `find` turns that into
   `{"ok":true,"items":[],"note":"ничего не найдено"}` and the plugin hint
   simply emits no block (both call the same `search()`).
3. **Relative noise floor** (see M5 § Threshold below; re-derived in M6) —
   **abolished in M7**, see § M7.

M6 amended steps 1–2: words are token-level (`next.js` stays one word, a
hyphen splits), `why` attributes a field by token equality, and upper-case
short acronyms became meaningful — see § M6.

**M7 amended step 2 and removed step 3**: the stop list became the standard
service-word list, and "at least one matched token" became the **coverage
rule** `matched ≥ min(2, N)`; the score floor (`MIN_STRENGTH` +
`corpusCeiling`) is gone — see § M7.

Stop words and short tokens are still indexed and still contribute to BM25
scores (scoring semantics were not part of M5); they only lose the right to
*prove* a match.

## Metrics (`run.mjs`)

Eligibility follows `baseline.mjs`: a query counts toward the retrieval
averages only if at least one qrel is present in the index; qrels absent from
the index are reported separately (`missingQrels`), never silently dropped.

- **recall@5** — share of eligible queries where at least one qrel is in the
  top-5.
- **all@5** — share of eligible queries where **all** (present) qrels are in the
  top-5.
- **NDCG@10** — binary relevance (qrel in the ranked top-10 = 1), ideal DCG over
  `min(|qrels present|, 10)` relevant items; averaged over eligible queries.
- **AC3** — for the 10 `empty` queries: how many returned a non-empty result,
  how many with `score > 0`, with the query ids.

Both the **product** (MiniSearch, `core/index.mjs`: pipeline above, field weights
below) and the **baseline** (independent BM25 k=1.2 b=0.7, `measure/baseline.mjs`,
no MiniSearch, no stemming, no gate — the unchanged reference) are scored on the
same set in the same run.

## M5 § Weights

Field weights were re-compared on set A with the final pipeline (gate +
stemming) via `measure/weights.mjs` — `search()` takes an optional `boost`
override, so candidates differ **only** in field weights:

| candidate | easy r@5 | easy a@5 | hard r@5 | hard a@5 | all r@5 | all a@5 | all ndcg@10 | AC3 non-empty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| name 3 / desc 2 / head 1 (M4) | 0.7714 | 0.7714 | 0.6000 | 0.2667 | 0.7200 | 0.6200 | 0.6161 | 2/10 |
| name 2 / desc 3 / head 1 | 0.7429 | 0.7429 | 0.6000 | 0.2667 | 0.7000 | 0.6000 | 0.5974 | 3/10 |
| name 1.5 / desc 3 / head 1 | 0.7429 | 0.7429 | 0.6000 | 0.2667 | 0.7000 | 0.6000 | 0.5871 | 3/10 |

Selection rule: highest recall@5 over all eligible queries, ties broken by
all@5 then NDCG@10, easy/hard must not regress against the incumbent. **Winner:
name ×3 / description ×2 / headings ×1** — it wins recall@5 *and* all@5, so the
M4 weights are kept (re-confirmed against two candidates, not assumed).

## M5 § Threshold (relative noise floor) — HISTORICAL, abolished by M7

> **M7 status:** this section and § M6 § Threshold describe a mechanism that
> **no longer exists**: M7 deleted `MIN_STRENGTH` and `corpusCeiling` and
> replaced the floor with the coverage rule (§ M7 § Rule). Kept verbatim as
> the record of how the 0.7 value was derived while it existed.

After the gate, leftovers still existed on A (9/10 non-empty), e.g. a doc whose
only overlap with «Как сварить борщ с говядиной» is the word «как». The floor:

```
ceiling(q) = Σ over meaningful tokens t of q of:
               best score of a one-term search for t in the corpus
               OR  (if t occurs in NO skill)  idf(df=0) · (d + k + 1) · max(field boost)
keep the result list only if  best_score(q) ≥ 0.7 · ceiling(q), else return []
```

Why this ceiling and not a constant score: BM25 scores are not comparable across
queries (idfs and token counts differ by an order of magnitude), so the cutoff is
made *relative to what this query could achieve in this corpus*. The theoretical
part (`idf(df=0)·(d+k+1)·maxBoost`, the exact BM25 saturation upper bound at
k=1.2, b=0.7, d=0.5) stops a query whose rare tokens are simply absent from the
corpus from getting a tiny denominator for free.

Why 0.7 and not a magic number — it is the measured separating gap of set A:

## M6 § Token-level match, words, acronyms

### Diagnosis (checked on the live index, not assumed)

Two claims were verified against the real corpus (365 skills) **before** any
code change:

1. **«the gate compares substrings» — REFUTED for the gate itself.** The
   `search()` gate compares normalized/stemmed tokens by *equality*
   (MiniSearch `r.match` keys are document terms from the same pipeline), so
   «bus» against the word «business» already answered `[]`
   (stems: `bus` → `bus`, `business` → `busin`, `abuse` → `abuse`).
2. **The substring really existed — in two other places:**
   - `why` field attribution used `text.includes(term)`: a skill named
     `Officer-training` with «office» only in its description was reported as
     `matched name+description: office` (false credit to `name`);
   - the tokenizer split on every non-alphanumeric character, so the written
     word **«Next.js»** handed out a free `next` token — in #58's returned
     skills «next» came ONLY from «Next.js» (build-recipes, gsap-react,
     edge-case-auditor).

Where each AC3 token actually occurs (indexed fields, *written* words with
their dots/hyphens):

| token | written words containing it | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `bus` | `Business`, `business`, `abuse`, `business-website-skill` | never a word of its own; **never matched** (proof above) |
| `airport` | — | absent from the corpus |
| `coffee` | — | absent from the corpus |
| `next` | `next`, `Next`, `next-steps`, `Next.js`, `Next.js-проекта`, `NextSlide`, `nextslide`, `React-Vue-Next` | mixed: standalone «next» exists; in #58's returned skills it came only from «Next.js» |
| `when` | `when`, `When`, `WHEN`, `whenever` | standalone — the real cause of #58 |
| `what` | `what`, `What`, `WHAT`, `whatever` | standalone — the real cause of #59 |
| `should` | `should`, `Should`, `SHOULD` | standalone — the real cause of #59 |
| `office` | `office`, `Office`, `Officer`, `officer` | standalone exists (`pep-screening`, `rospatent-application`) *and* inside «Officer» |

So #58/#59 are **not** substring artifacts: they survive on genuine
token-equal occurrences of function-like English words (`when`, `next`,
`what`, `should`). The leftovers are semantic noise, not lexical noise.

### Word rule (the implementation)

A **word** is a run of letters/digits that may contain a **dot**, never a
**hyphen** (`core/text.mjs` `tokenize`); the gate and `why` count a match only
when a normalized/stemmed query token is **equal** to a word of the skill text.

- **dot stays inside the word**: `next.js` is one word → `next` ∌ `next.js`
  (required test), while the query «next.js» still matches the same text —
  the rule is identical on both sides. The whole-word query folds as
  `next.js` → `nextjs` → stem `nextj`.
- **hyphen splits the word**: `gsap` **does** match `gsap-scrolltrigger`
  (required decision — a hyphen joins independent words: `gsap-scrolltrigger`,
  `next-steps`, and it is the boundary in mixed-script compounds like
  `AI-документ`, which would otherwise become one unusable token). Tested in
  `test/ac3.test.mjs`.

Source of truth: the product specification (`spec.md` §5 R1–R6, §6 tool
contracts, §7 hint contract), owner decisions of 25.10.2026 (§4), the owner
decision of 26.10.2026 to split search from the hint (v0.3: `find` returns the
full list with a `confident` flag), the owner decision of 26.10.2026
«Передавай» / «5 кандидатов» (v0.4: the hint and `find` present **up to 5
candidates**, confident first, unconfirmed ones marked «(возможно)» —
the MCP no longer claims a single answer) and the
owner decision of 26.10.2026 choosing **variant G** of the variants lab
(v0.4.1: query expansion + `BOOST_ORDER` domain boost inside `search()`,
tool-silence + confident gate in the hint, `find` default limit 10 — the
lab's G behaviour ported verbatim, metrics in `measure/README.md` § v0.4.1).
Owner task 27.10.2026 (**v0.6.2**): the note now tells the agent to read the
candidate descriptions and load the matching skill, and every non-empty
`find` answer carries a top-level `next`.
The English text below is a faithful summary; where the specification wording
matters, the original Russian text is quoted verbatim. Companion to
the [README](../README.md).

## R1–R6 (requirements)

**R1 — the hint never claims a skill is loaded.** The block always carries the
wrapper below (v0.6.2 note wording, owner task 27.10.2026).

> **R1.** Подсказка НИКОГДА не утверждает, что скилл загружен; формулировка вида
> `<skill_hint source="skill-router" note="посмотри описания кандидатов; если один подходит — загрузи его через skill; если нет — не загружай.">`.

**R2 — allow/deny is the plugin config; default is everything except the
forbidden list** (redaction per the owner's decision, spec §4 п. 5).

> **R2.** Подсказка соблюдает allowlist имён скиллов (редакция по решению владельца, §4, п. 5):
> подсказываются любые скиллы, кроме запрещённых списком в конфиге плагина.

**R3 — the hint does not replace the lead's mandatory «Скиллы» field.**

> **R3.** Подсказка НЕ заменяет обязательное поле «Скиллы» в ответе лида и не считается
> его выполнением.

**R4 — the hint does not affect the skill-gate lock.**

> **R4.** Подсказка не влияет на замок skill-gate: гейт считает только реальные вызовы
> инструмента `skill`.

**R5 — fully local, read-only.**

> **R5.** Полностью локально: без сети, LLM, ключей, телеметрии; чтение файлов скиллов —
> только чтение.

**R6 — fail-open and the hint budget.**

> **R6.** Fail-open: любой сбой подсказки не ломает сессию; выключение одной env-переменной
> убирает подсказку целиком; бюджет — не более 1000 символов, не более 2 позиций,
> не более 150 мс.

v0.4 amendment (owner decision 26.10.2026): the position budget is **5
candidates** instead of 2; 1000 chars and 150 ms are unchanged.

v0.4.1 amendment (owner decision 26.10.2026, variant G): the budgets stay
exactly as above (≤5 / ≤1000 / ≤150 ms — G does not widen them, the lab's
10-entry option was NOT chosen); what changed is WHEN a block forms: a
**tool-silence** check (a complaint about the plugin/router/MCP itself → no
block) and a **confident gate** (no `confident:true` position in the
top-10 pool → no block) run before the budget is even spent. The R6 budgets
for a possible 10-entry variant remain an owner-open question (lab §8 (б)).

## Hint block format

Mandatory wrapper (R1, verbatim, v0.6.2 note):

```text
<skill_hint source="skill-mcp" note="посмотри описания кандидатов; если один подходит — загрузи его через skill; если нет — не загружай.">
- <skill-name>: <one line why>; открыть: инструмент skill, name=<skill-name>
- <skill-name> (возможно): <one line why>; открыть: инструмент skill, name=<skill-name>
</skill_hint>
```

- up to **5 candidates** (v0.4, owner decision 26.10.2026: «5 кандидатов»);
  each candidate = skill name, one «why» line taken from `description` (first
  line, ≤120 chars), and how to open it (`skill` tool, `name=…`);
- **confident first**: `confident:true` positions (≥ `min(2, N)` significant
  query tokens covered) always precede `confident:false` ones (the v0.3.1
  order of `search()`); a candidate that did not pass the coverage rule is
  marked **«(возможно)»** right after its name — the marker names the
  uncertainty instead of hiding the candidate. v0.4.1 exception: the domain
  boost of `search()` runs after that order on `BOOST_TRIGGER` queries and
  may move a `BOOST_ORDER` name to position 1 (measured: it is `confident`
  on Q1/Q3 anyway);
- **two silences before the block (v0.4.1, variant G)**:
  1. **tool-silence** — the query matches BOTH a tool word
     (`плагин|skill-router|skill-mcp|mcp`) and a complaint word
     («почему|не нашел|не нашёл|не активировал|не работает») → no block: the
     model answers the user's question about the tool, candidates would be
     noise;
  2. **confident gate** — the pool (the top-10 of `search()`) contains no
     `confident:true` position → no block. Unconfirmed candidates may appear
     only behind at least one proven one (still marked «(возможно)»);
- **the block states candidates, never a single answer**: the note instructs
  verbatim «посмотри описания кандидатов; если один подходит — загрузи его
  через skill; если нет — не загружай.» — read the candidate descriptions,
  load the one that matches, load nothing when none fits. AC3
  («no random hints») is therefore rephrased as **«кандидаты, не утверждение»**
  — the block must present options, not assert which skill is THE one; a
  hint block forms as long as the search found anything that survives
  deny/allow and the name/description sanity checks AND the two silences
  above pass;
- the whole block **≤ 1000 characters** (R6) ≈ ≤ 250 tokens (chars / 4; the
  lab's Cyrillic/3 + Latin/4 estimate for a typical 4-entry block: ~194–202
  tokens); if the 5th candidate does not fit, the tail is **dropped** (the
  block keeps what fits — it is never replaced by an empty block);
- forbidden: claiming the skill is loaded/opened (R1); quoting skill bodies;
  more than 5 candidates or 1000 chars; asserting one candidate as the
  answer; passing itself off as the «Скиллы» field or its execution (R3);
  generating any tool call, including `skill` (R4); reading files outside the
  skill roots; network, LLM, keys, telemetry (R5).

Default behaviour (owner decision §4 п. 5): every skill is hintable except the
agent's `deny` list in the plugin config; an `allow` list per agent narrows it
to those names. The hint acts in all sessions, including subagents (§4 п. 6).

## Tool contracts (MCP server, stdio / JSON-RPC 2.0)

Common: every answer is a JSON object `{ok, …}`; every error is
`{ok:false, error:{code, message}}`; all tools read files only inside the
skill roots after resolving the canonical path (path traversal is refused —
AC4).

### `find`

v0.3 (owner decision 26.10.2026 — search split from the hint), v0.4
(candidate list) and **v0.4.1 (variant G)**: `find`
returns **up to `limit` candidates** (**default 10** since v0.4.1); the
coverage rule does not filter the list and only flags each position, every
item carries the skill `description` so the model can judge the candidates
without extra calls, and the query goes through the G pipeline inside
`search()` (see «Query processing» below) — `find` receives expansion and
domain boost automatically.

Tool description (v0.6.2): it leads with «Call this FIRST», says the call
returns a shortlist with each skill's description, tells the model to **read
the descriptions and choose the skill that matches**, to verify a
`confident:true` likely match against its description, and to **load the
chosen skill with the `skill` tool before answering** — or proceed without a
skill when no candidate matches.

| | |
|---|---|
| Input | `query: string` (required), `limit?: integer` (default **10** since v0.4.1, **max 10**), `restrict_to?: string[]` (skill-name / glob allowlist filter) |
| Answer | `{ok:true, items:[{name, path, score, why, description, confident}], next}` sorted by descending `score` (confident first); `why` — one line, ≤160 chars; `description` — the skill's frontmatter description ("" when absent); `confident: boolean` — the position covers ≥ `min(2, N)` significant query tokens (N = the number of the EXPANDED query's meaningful tokens — v0.4.1), i.e. it is a proven rather than a possible candidate; `next` (top-level, since v0.6.2) — `likely match: <name> — verify its description and load it` when the first item is `confident:true`, otherwise `review the candidate descriptions; load the matching skill`; empty results carry no `next` (there is nothing to review) |
| Index fields | `name` (×3), `description` (×2), `headings` (×1), **`aliases` (×1)** — the v0.2 bilingual bridge: RU↔EN dictionary equivalents of the document's own terms, written at index time from the static `core/lexicon.ru-en.json` (local file only, no network/LLM, R5); the confidence rule (≥`min(2, N)` significant tokens by token equality) applies to alias matches like any other token, except the weak pairs listed in `core/lexicon.ru-en.json` under `_weak` — those rank but never count toward confidence (v0.2.1) |
| Query processing (v0.4.1, G) | inside `search()`: **expansion** — a query containing «описан…» appends «текст», «продукт…» appends « product» (`expandQuery`); tokens, the `confident` coverage check and `why` run on the EXPANDED query; **domain boost** — when the ORIGINAL query matches `BOOST_TRIGGER` = `описан\|текст\|лендинг\|копирайт\|продукт`, the capped pool is reordered so `BOOST_ORDER` = promo, copywriting, site-copywriting, app-copywriting, documentation-and-adrs, redpolitika leads it (`boostReorder`) — **reorder only, no additions**; the name list is hardcoded (owner-open question, README §8) |
| Limits | ≤10 items; ≤1 `why` line per item; other fields truncated |
| Empty query | `{ok:true, items:[], note:"пустой запрос"}` |
| No hits at all | `{ok:true, items:[], note:"ничего не найдено"}` |
| Hits, none confident | `{ok:true, items:[{…, confident:false}, …], note:"уверенных нет, вот возможные"}` — the candidate list is still returned (v0.3/v0.4) |
| Errors | `E_INVALID_INPUT` (not a string, `limit` outside 1–10 — rejected, not clamped), `E_UNAVAILABLE` (skill directory unavailable / index not built; the call fails, opencode still starts) |

**AC3 caveat (v0.4 rephrasing, owner decision 26.10.2026).** AC3 —
«no random hints» — is now **«кандидаты, не утверждение»**: both consumers
present candidates rather than asserting an answer. The `find` output is a
ranked candidate list (`confident` per item, `note` when nothing is
confident, `next` telling the agent to verify and load); the plugin hint
shows the same candidates (≤5, «(возможно)» on unconfirmed ones) and its
note reads verbatim «посмотри описания кандидатов; если один подходит —
загрузи его через skill; если нет — не загружай.» — read the descriptions,
load the matching skill, or load nothing when none fits.

### `outline`

| | |
|---|---|
| Input | `name: string` (skill name) **or** `path: string` (checked to be inside a skill root) |
| Answer | `{ok:true, name, path, description, headings:[{level, text, line}]}` — frontmatter plus H1–H3 headings with line numbers |
| Limits | ≤40 headings, ≤150 answer lines; overflow → cut from the bottom and `truncated:true` |
| Errors | `E_INVALID_INPUT` (empty/missing input), `E_NOT_FOUND` (unknown skill), `E_FORBIDDEN` (outside the skill roots) |

### `read-section`

| | |
|---|---|
| Input | `name: string` (required), `heading: string \| integer` (heading text without `#`, or its number in `outline` order), `max_lines?: integer` (default 150, **max 600**) |
| Answer | `{ok:true, name, heading, line_start, lines:[...], truncated:boolean}` — from the heading to the next heading of the same level |
| Limits | ≤600 lines per answer; longer sections truncated with `truncated:true` |
| Errors | `E_INVALID_INPUT`, `E_NOT_FOUND` (skill), `E_SECTION_NOT_FOUND` (heading), `E_FORBIDDEN` (outside the skill roots) |

Transport-level JSON-RPC codes (not tool-level): unknown tool `-32602`,
unknown method `-32601`, malformed line `-32700`, invalid request `-32600`,
unexpected failure `-32603`.

## Safety guarantees

- **Read-only**: the product never writes, moves or deletes any file; the
  index is built in memory from `SKILL.md` frontmatter and headings.
- **No network**: no HTTP, no LLM, no embeddings, no API keys, no telemetry
  (R5) — the MCP server talks stdio, the plugin runs BM25 over the local
  index.
- **Root boundary**: every path is resolved to its canonical real path
  (realpath) and must stay inside one of the skill roots; anything outside is
  refused with `E_FORBIDDEN` (`resolveSkillPath` in `core/sources.mjs`,
  symlink escapes reported as `skipped: outside-root`).
- **No side effects in opencode**: the plugin appends exactly one `system`
  text part per request (≤5 candidates, ≤1000 chars) and touches nothing else —
  messages, history, tools and options are unchanged; it never calls the
  `skill` tool, so it cannot create skill-gate events (R3, R4).
- **Fail-open** (R6): any internal error drops the hint instead of failing the
  request; `SKILL_MCP_HINT=off|0|false` removes the hint completely (the legacy
  `SKILL_ROUTER_HINT` name is deprecated since v0.5.0 and still works as a
  fallback when the new variable is unset; with both set, `SKILL_MCP_HINT`
  wins).
- **No LLM / no embeddings / no network, still true for v0.4.1**: the G
  expansion and boost are two regexes and one hardcoded name list inside
  `core/index.mjs` — no model call, no external data, read-only local files
  (R5; `test/safety.test.mjs` keeps scanning core for network imports).
